rules.title: California Civil Code Section 1950.6 (tenant screening fees)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a capped screening fee only for actual costs, must give a receipt, itemization, credit report copy and refund of unused fees, and may not charge when no unit is available. They must use a reusable screening report if the tenant provides one, and either refund fees to applicants not selected or review applications in order received.
rules.status_basis: Described as current state law on the Berkeley Rent Board page

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords charging screening fees to prospective tenants of residential rentals.

rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.

rules.title: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.78 (Tenant Screening and Application Fees)
rules.requirement: Owners who charge a screening fee must give a clear tenant screening fee rights statement and the state maximum fee cap before receiving the fee. Owners may not charge existing tenants non-refundable fees for renewing a tenancy or for roommate departures or additions, and the chapter overrides contrary lease terms.

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley regardless of contrary lease language.

rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
